rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It contains the same distinctive sugar-quota proposal: congressional authorization for the President to adjust foreign quotas when required by the national interest or adequate domestic sugar supplies. The child condenses and reuses that machinery and phrasing while urging prompt action on the same Administration legislation. C21 and C23 share appeals for congressional action on Administration agricultural legislation, but lack the distinctive sugar-quota mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the President be given appropriate authority to adjust certain foreign quotas when he finds such action is called for--either in the national interest or to insure adequate domestic supplies of sugar
shared_material.parent_excerpt: give me the authority to reduce the quota for a calendar year for any foreign country ... when I determine it to be in the national interest or necessary to insure adequate supplies of sugar
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim formulation of the proposed presidential authority, its foreign-quota target, and its two triggering standards.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hope most earnestly that Congress will act promptly on the sugar legislation recommended last March by this Administration
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Accordingly, I have recommended to the Congress only certain minimum changes in the present Sugar Act. The most important of these would give me the authority
shared_material.explanation: Both present the quota-adjustment authority as the central component of the Administration's pending sugar legislation and place enactment in Congress's hands.
